## The problem

A target phenotype, such as a metabolite, is measured on only part of a cohort.
Complete-case analysis of its association with an exposure uses only the
participants who have it. Synthetic surrogate (SynSurr) analysis gains precision
by modelling the target jointly with a *synthetic phenotype*, a prediction of
the target from other variables (*surrogates*), which is available where the
target is missing. MultiSynSurr uses several synthetic phenotypes built from
different surrogates, each available on its own subset, as separate outcomes of
one multivariate model.

## Example

`msr_simulate()` generates a cohort in which 30% of participants are assayed and
have a first synthetic phenotype `S1` (accurate), a quarter of them have the
target measured, and everyone has a second synthetic phenotype `S2` (weaker).

```{r}
library(MultiSynSurr)
d <- msr_simulate(n = 10000, seed = 1)
colMeans(!is.na(cbind(target = d$target, d$synthetic)))
```

Fit MultiSynSurr with both synthetic phenotypes and test the exposure:

```{r}
fit <- msr(d$target, d$synthetic, d$X)
fit
msr_test(fit, "exposure")
```

Compare with complete-case least squares and with the precision gain predicted
from the fitted covariance and the missingness patterns:

```{r}
o <- !is.na(d$target)
cc <- summary(lm(d$target[o] ~ d$X[o, ]))$coefficients
se_cc <- cc[nrow(cc), "Std. Error"]
c(observed = msr_test(fit, "exposure")[["se"]] / se_cc,
  predicted = sqrt(msr_expected_ratio(fit)))
```

## Points to observe

* Each synthetic phenotype must be built the same way for every participant and
  must not use the variable whose association is tested. Its accuracy affects
  only the precision, not the validity.
* Pass synthetic phenotypes built from different surrogates as separate columns.
  Merging them into one column makes the synthetic phenotype a different
  variable where the target is measured than where it is missing, and biases the
  estimate.
* The model assumes the target is missing at random given the design and the
  synthetic phenotypes.
